record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: Can ferromagnet/spin-glass or antiferromagnet/spin-glass interfaces form during fabrication of van der Waals magnetic systems, and can such interfaces induce exchange bias?

evidence.quote: vii. Can FM/SG or AFM/SG interfaces be formed during fabrication and induce the EB effect in vdW magnetic systems?

artifact.category_tag: van der Waals magnetic heterostructures / exchange bias
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider heterostructures built from two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic materials, in which atomically thin layers exhibiting ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) order are stacked together. A spin glass (SG) is a magnetic phase characterized by frozen, randomly oriented spins arising from quenched disorder and competing exchange interactions, typically associated with interfacial intermixing, defects, or chemical disorder. The exchange bias (EB) effect refers to a horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop along the field axis, conventionally attributed to interfacial exchange coupling between magnetically ordered phases (e.g., FM/AFM bilayers) after field cooling through an ordering temperature.

Determine whether, during the fabrication (e.g., exfoliation, stacking, growth, or transfer) of two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic heterostructures, interfaces of the form ferromagnet/spin-glass (FM/SG) or antiferromagnet/spin-glass (AFM/SG) can be formed, and whether such interfaces can induce the exchange bias effect. Provide either a demonstration (theoretical or experimental in principle) that such interfaces arise and produce exchange bias, or arguments showing this mechanism cannot operate in the van der Waals setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of the open questions about exchange bias in 2D van der Waals magnetic heterostructures. While spin-glass-like behavior and exchange bias have been reported in several vdW systems (e.g., CrPS3, Fe3GeTe2-based junctions), a direct, conclusive identification of fabrication-induced FM/SG or AFM/SG interfaces as the origin of exchange bias in vdW heterostructures has not been firmly established in the literature as of the search date. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions and perspectives concerning exchange bias in vdW magnetic systems, including the possible role of spin-glass interfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question of FM/SG and AFM/SG interface formation and induced exchange bias in vdW heterostructures is listed as an open question.
